objective: Standard statement: counting the colourings of connected cubic bipartite Pfaffian graphs under arbitrary signings is #P-hard, already for planar cubic bipartite hosts carrying trisum junctions of twisted truncated-octahedron pages (branched twists). Proof by reduction from #Positive-NAE-3SAT (#P-complete, Creignou-Hermann 1996): clauses are host lines; a variable of degree d is a tree of host points joined by merge wires (planar paths of host lines, Hadamard signature [3^k, 0, (-1)^k], interpolated to equality); crossings of the drawing are snake sites (ticket A); spare legs are capped; instances are Pfaffian by the gauge lemma of SEYMOUR-COUNT A; polynomially many oracle calls and a two-parameter Vandermonde system. Demonstrated end to end on a small instance. Nearest known result: Creignou-Hermann; holographic and interpolation reductions. Classification: to be decided.
status: Proved: counting colourings of cubic bipartite Pfaffian graphs under signings is #P-hard (Turing); oracle instances have three twisted branches at every junction, while the knot's class and unbranched twists count in polynomial time. Source (known, Fan-Cai 2020) replayed by merge paths and dead caps; six formulas recovered exactly.
title: Counting under branched twists is #P-hard
